course: CSE 3103 - Database Management Systems (AUST, Semester Final)

questions.text: Define a database management system. List four advantages of a DBMS over a traditional file-processing system.
Explain the three-schema architecture of a DBMS. Describe the two levels of data independence it provides.
Draw an ER diagram for a university course-registration system covering students, courses, sections and instructors. Mark all cardinality and participation constraints.
Map the ER diagram of Question 3 into a set of relational schemas. Clearly identify the primary key and foreign keys of every relation.

Consider Enrollment(student_id, course_id, semester, grade, instructor_name, instructor_dept) with FDs: student_id, course_id, semester -> grade; course_id, semester -> instructor_name; instructor_name -> instructor_dept. Normalise the relation up to 3NF, showing each intermediate step.

Using the schema Student(id, name, dept, cgpa) and Enrollment(id, course_id, grade), write SQL statements to: (a) list students with CGPA above 3.50 ordered by CGPA, (b) count enrolments per department, (c) find students who have never enrolled in any course.
State the ACID properties of a transaction. Briefly explain each property with a suitable example.
Explain conflict serializability and view serializability. Give one example schedule that is view serializable but not conflict serializable.
